execution_paths.summary: FUNC-INIT ('INIT'): open both files, build the in-memory process table from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE records of the requested sequence type, write one READY control record per process to BATCH-CONTROL-FILE, return

FUNC-NEXT ('NEXT'): find the first READY process in the table, check its dependencies against BATCH-CONTROL-FILE; if all satisfied (LS-RETURN-CODE = 0) mark its control record ACTIVE with a start time; return the process ID in LS-NEXT-PROCESS
FUNC-STAT ('STAT'): read the control record of LS-NEXT-PROCESS, copy its status and return code into the table entry, recount active and error processes, return
FUNC-TERM ('TERM'): recount active/error processes, set LS-RETURN-CODE to error (8) if any errors, warning (4) if any still active, else success (0); close both files, return
Any other LS-FUNCTION value: ERR-TEXT = 'Invalid function code', 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE sets LS-RETURN-CODE = BCT-RC-ERROR (8) and calls ERRPROC, return

trace_issues.name: WS-SUB
trace_issues.message: WS-SUB is used as the PERFORM VARYING index and as a subscript of PSR-DEP-ID / PSR-DEP-HARD / PSR-DEP-RC but has no declaration in scope; the program would not compile as written

PERFORM UNTIL WS-PSR-STATUS = '10' (line 168): only AT END (or a READ returning status '10') ends the loop. If START fails (INVALID KEY, line 163) processing continues into the loop, and a READ NEXT that keeps returning a non-'10' error status would repeat indefinitely
1210-ADD-TO-SEQUENCE increments index WS-PROC-IX with no check against WS-PROC-ENTRY OCCURS 100; more than 100 matching sequence records would write past the table
PSR-DEP-COUNT is PIC 9(2) COMP (up to 99) while PSR-DEP-ENTRY OCCURS 10 times; a dependency count above 10 would subscript past the table
9000-ERROR-ROUTINE sets LS-RETURN-CODE = BCT-RC-ERROR and calls ERRPROC, then returns to the performing paragraph; processing continues after every error (e.g. reads after a failed open)

LS-RETURN-CODE is never reset at the start of a call; on paths without errors (INIT, NEXT, STAT) the value returned is whatever the caller passed in or an earlier assignment left. In 2200 the dependency loop exits on the first iteration if LS-RETURN-CODE is already non-zero on entry

MOVE LS-PROCESS-DATE (X(8)) TO PSR-KEY (group: PSR-PROCESS-ID X(8) + PSR-VERSION 9(2)) positions PROCESS-SEQ-FILE by a date value in the process-ID part of the key; START KEY >= then reads all following records and filters only on PSR-TYPE
2200 sets only PSR-PROCESS-ID before the random READ; PSR-VERSION (the rest of RECORD KEY PSR-KEY) keeps whatever the record area holds
MOVE WS-CURRENT-TIME (X(26), timestamp) TO BCT-START-TIME (X(8)) keeps only the first 8 characters
When 2100 finds no READY process it sets LS-NEXT-PROCESS to spaces, but 2000 still performs 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES, which reads PROCESS-SEQ-FILE with a blank key (INVALID KEY -> 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE)
Static CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE: ERRPROC is not in this batch's PROGRAM_FILTER, so its logic summary was not available

program_narrative: Program PRCSEQ00 is a batch process-sequence manager subroutine. The caller passes a request (LS-SEQUENCE-REQUEST) whose function code selects one of four services. INIT opens the process-sequence file (PROCESS-SEQ-FILE) and the batch control file (BATCH-CONTROL-FILE), loads every process definition of the requested sequence type into an in-memory table of up to 100 entries, and writes one READY batch-control record per process for the processing date. NEXT returns the first READY process, checks each of its dependencies against the batch control file (a hard dependency that is not done gives a warning return code; a done dependency whose return code exceeds the allowed limit gives an error return code) and, when all checks pass, marks the process ACTIVE with a start time. STAT reads the control record of a process, copies its status and return code into the table and recounts active and failed processes. TERM sets the final return code (8 if any process failed, 4 if any is still active, otherwise 0) and closes both files. Any other function code, and every file error, goes through 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, which sets return code 8 and calls the external error program ERRPROC; processing then continues. Open review items: the loop subscript WS-SUB is undeclared, the sequence table and dependency table have no bounds checks, and the build loop depends only on end-of-file to stop.

POSITION PROCESS-SEQ-FILE at first record with key >= psr_key  -- START
IF no such record THEN  -- INVALID KEY

WHILE ws_psr_status != '10' DO  -- PERFORM UNTIL ... END-PERFORM (inline loop); '10' = end of file

paragraphs.name: 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS
pseudocode: -- Check one dependency (entry ws_sub) against its batch-control record
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key  -- job name + process date (+ sequence no.)
IF record not found THEN  -- INVALID KEY
IF dependency job is not done THEN  -- NOT BCT-STATUS-DONE: bct_status != 'D'
IF dependency is hard THEN  -- PSR-DEP-HARD(ws_sub): psr_dep_type = 'H'
IF bct_return_code > psr_dep_rc[ws_sub] THEN  -- finished with a worse return code than allowed
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Check one dependency (entry ws_sub) against its batch-control record
SET bct_job_name = psr_dep_id[ws_sub]
SET bct_process_date = ls_process_date
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key  -- job name + process date (+ sequence no.)
IF record not found THEN  -- INVALID KEY
  SET err_text = 'Dependency record not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
IF dependency job is not done THEN  -- NOT BCT-STATUS-DONE: bct_status != 'D'
  IF dependency is hard THEN  -- PSR-DEP-HARD(ws_sub): psr_dep_type = 'H'
    SET ls_return_code = bct_rc_warning  -- constant +4
  END IF
ELSE
  IF bct_return_code > psr_dep_rc[ws_sub] THEN  -- finished with a worse return code than allowed
    SET ls_return_code = bct_rc_error  -- constant +8
  END IF
END IF
